messages:
Mia (CS): Orca's reserved pool is green for tonight. Final warmup window 11:30 PT — can we run priming + a 30m soak? Need quota check and autoscale policy review.
Sam (Eng): Yep. Plan: run priming script `scripts/prime_orca.sh` with pattern ~95% short ctx, ~5% long (8k). Will validate KV cache hits and prefix warming. I'll push a short load profile as a k8s job.
Leo (SRE): On SRE side I'll open the reserve firewall rules and pre-allocate capacity tokens. What QPM do we aim for? Also will add token-rate alarms and extra log retention for the window.
Mia (CS): Orca requested 5k qps baseline, 10k burst for 5m. Their committed sustained target is 6k. They asked for <150ms p95 if possible. Confirming committed quota number now with the account team.
Sam (Eng): We can't safely hit 10k qps with autoscale min=4. I'll change autoscale to min=6, max=20 and put burst_policy=gradual+burst. Enable warmup_preload=true so model KV cache is primed during ramp. Deploy changes to staging first.
Leo (SRE): Add healthchecks `/health` and `/v1/status`, token-rate monitor `quota.tokens_used_per_min`. I'll make dashboard reserved/orca/priming and wire up alert runbooks. ops-bot, can you create an incident channel for the run?
ops-bot: Created #incident-orca-warmup and scheduled the run at 2024-11-12T18:30Z (11:30 PT). Notifying on-call.
Ryan (PM): Quick product note: capture p50/p95/p99 and fallback counts (model variant fallbacks, region fallbacks). If quality regression >2% on the eval set, abort and rollback.
Sam (Eng): Load command we'll use:
```
k6 run --vus 200 --duration 30m --rps 5000 scripts/orca_traffic.js
```
Will orchestrate from three regions: us-west1, us-central1, eu-west1 to exercise routing.
Mia (CS): I'll coordinate with Orca's success lead (cc: @OrcaOps) and confirm their SRE will be on call. They'll run smoke checks for auth/key rotation and do a quick sanity of cached prefixes.
Leo (SRE): Pre-populate model cache with the prefixes list: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/prime -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d @prefixes.json`. Metric to watch: `cache.kv_hit_rate` and `request.latency.p95`.
Sam (Eng): Important: if we hit quota caps, current behavior is to fallback to shared pool. For this warmup we want to block fallback for the first 10m to avoid noisy neighbor interference. I'll set routing policy strict -> reserved for the run window.
Mia (CS): Ops checklist for tonight: 1) confirm reserved quota numbers, 2) flip autoscale to planned values, 3) schedule priming job, 4) open #incident-orca-warmup, 5) postmortem template prepared.
Ryan (PM): Postmortem owner: Sam. CS will collect enablement feedback from Orca about onboarding docs, perceived latency, and any surprises in the console.
Sam (Eng): Acknowledged. I'll start the prereq changes at 11:00 PT and post step updates in #incident-orca-warmup.
Mia (CS): Perfect — thanks team :thumbsup:  I'll ping Orca 30m before kickoff to confirm their on-call.
